answer.summary: Thumbtack’s rapid growth masked a supply-side liquidity problem: it was generating demand it couldn’t adequately match with available professionals, leaving demand unserved.

sections.heading: The problem growth initially masked
sections.content: Lovinsky says Thumbtack had triple-digit growth while it was burning through demand: there wasn’t sufficient liquidity on the supply side to meet it, so the company was “dropping a lot of demand on the floor.” The team knew about the issue, but rapid growth made it seem less urgent; it became more visible when growth slowed and then turned negative.
